questions.text: A bullet of mass 20 g has an initial speed of 1 ms^(-1), just before it starts penetrating a mud wall of thickness 20 cm. If the wall offers a mean resistance of 2.5 × 10^(-2) N, the speed of the bullet after emerging from the other side of the wall is close to:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle starts from the origin at time t = 0 and moves along the positive x-axis. The graph of velocity with respect to time is shown in figure. What is the position of the particle at time t = 5s ?
questions.sol_text:
Area under v-t curve gives displacement.
A = 2 + 4 + 3 = 9 = ΔS
ΔS = x_f - x_i = 9 - 0 = 9
So, final position is x = 9 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle is moving with speed v = b*sqrt(x) along positive x-axis. Calculate the speed of the particle at time t = tau (assume that the particle is at origin t = 0)
questions.sol_text:
v = b*sqrt(x)

dx/dt = b*x^(1/2) => integral from 0 to x of x^(-1/2) dx = integral from 0 to tau of b dt

=> 2*sqrt(x_tau) = b*tau => sqrt(x_tau) = b*tau/2

v_tau = b*sqrt(x_tau) = b*(b*tau/2) = b^2*tau/2

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A passenger train of length 60 m travels at a speed of 80 km/hr. Another freight train of length 120 m travels at a speed of 30 km/hr. The ratio of times taken by the passenger train to completely cross the freight train when : (i) they are moving in the same direction, and (ii) in the opposite direction is :
questions.sol_text:
Trains are moving in same direction

Distance to be covered = 60 m + 120 m = 180 m

Relative speed of passenger train = 80 - 30 = 50 km/h

T1 = 180/50

Trains are moving in opposite direction

Relative speed of train = 80 + 30 = 110 km/h

T2 = 180/110

T1/T2 = (180/50)/(180/110) = 110/50 = 11/5

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle starts from origin O from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration along the positive x-axis. Identify all figures that correctly represent the motion qualitatively. (a = acceleration, v = velocity, x = displacement, t = time)
questions.sol_text:
a = constant

For uniform acceleration starting from rest:

v ∝ t
Since v = at and a is constant, velocity increases linearly with time.
Figure (B) shows v increasing linearly with t - CORRECT

x ∝ t^2
Since x = (1/2)at^2 and a is constant, displacement increases as the square of time (parabolic curve).
Figure (D) shows x increasing parabolically with t - CORRECT

For acceleration:
a = constant (positive, non-zero)
Figure (A) shows a as constant with respect to t - CORRECT

Therefore, the figures that correctly represent the motion are (A), (B), and (D).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The position of a particle as a function of time t, is given by x(t) = at + bt^2 - ct^3 where a, b and c are constants. When the particle attains zero acceleration, then its velocity will be:
questions.sol_text:
x = at + bt^2 - ct^3
v = a + 2bt - 3ct^2
acceleration = 2b - 6ct = 0
t = 2b/(6c) = b/(3c)

so velocity at t = b/(3c)
v = a + 2b(b/(3c)) - 3c(b/(3c))^2
v = a + 2b^2/(3c) - 3c(b^2/(9c^2))
v = a + 2b^2/(3c) - 3b^2/(9c)
v = a + 2b^2/(3c) - b^2/(3c)
v = a + b^2/(3c)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A ball is thrown vertically up (taken as + z-axis) from the ground. The correct momentum-height (p-h) diagram is:
options: Graph showing p vs h with curve starting at origin, going upward to the right, then curving downward
Graph showing p vs h with curve starting at origin, going upward to the right in a parabolic shape
Graph showing p vs h with curve starting at origin, going upward with decreasing slope, forming a parabola opening leftward
Graph showing p vs h with curve starting at origin, going upward with decreasing slope, forming a parabola opening leftward (similar to option 3)
questions.sol_text:
When thrown upward, (h = 0) V → max
V^2 = u^2 + 2as
V^2 = u^2 - 2gh (Parabola)
When downward (h → max, V → 0)

Momentum p = mV
p^2 = m^2 V^2 = m^2(u^2 - 2gh)
p^2 = m^2 u^2 - 2m^2 gh

This is a parabolic relationship between p^2 and h.
At h = 0: p = mu (maximum momentum)
As h increases: p decreases
At maximum height: p = 0

The relationship is: p^2 = m^2 u^2 - 2m^2 gh

Rearranging: p^2 + 2m^2 gh = m^2 u^2
This represents a parabola opening leftward (in the negative p direction) on a p-h diagram.

Therefore, the diagram should show:
- Curve starting at maximum p at h = 0
- p decreasing as h increases
- Parabolic shape with the curve bending toward the h-axis
- When h reaches maximum, p = 0

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In a car race on straight road, car A takes a time t less than car B at the finish and passes finishing point with a speed 'v' more than that of car B. Both the cars start from rest and travel with constant acceleration a1 and a2 respectively. Then 'v' is equal to:
questions.sol_text:
S = (1/2)*a1*t0^2 = (1/2)*a2*(t0+t)^2

v = (sqrt(a1) - sqrt(a2)) × sqrt(2*S)

((1/sqrt(a2)) - (1/sqrt(a1))) × sqrt(2*S) = t

sqrt(2*S) = (sqrt(a1)*sqrt(a2)*t)/(sqrt(a1) - sqrt(a2))

v/(sqrt(a1) - sqrt(a2)) = (sqrt(a1)*sqrt(a2)*t)/((sqrt(a1) - sqrt(a2)))

v = sqrt(a1*a2)*t

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Train A and train B are running on parallel tracks in the opposite directions with speeds of 36 km/hour and 72 km/hour, respectively. A person is walking in train A in the direction opposite to its motion with a speed of 1.8 km/hr. Speed (in ms^(-1)) of this person as observed from train B will be close to: (take the distance between the tracks as negligible)
questions.sol_text:
Velocity of man with respect to ground
vector V_m/g = vector V_m/A + vector V_A = -1.8 + 36

Velocity of man w.r.t. B
vector V_m/B = vector V_m - vector V_B
= -1.8 + 36 - (-72)
= 106.2 km/hr
= 29.5 m/s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A Tennis ball is released from a height h and after freely falling on a wooden floor it rebounds and reaches height h/2. The velocity versus height of the ball during its motion may be represented graphically by: (graph are drawn schematically and on not to scale)
options: Graph (1): Shows v vs h(v) with curve starting near h/2 on h-axis, curving down through origin, and extending to h
Graph (2): Shows v vs h(v) with curve starting at h on h-axis, curving down to h/2
Graph (3): Shows v vs h(v) with loop-like curve between 0 and h, with h/2 marked
Graph (4): Shows v vs h(v) with straight line from h/2 to h on h-axis
questions.sol_text:
Velocity at ground (means zero height) is non-zero therefore one is incorrect and velocity versus height is non-linear therefore two is also incorrect.

Using energy conservation: v^2 = 2gh

Taking derivative: v(dv/dh) = 2g = constant

Therefore: dv/dh = constant/v

Here we can see slope is very high when velocity is low therefore at Maximum height the slope should be very large which is in option 2 and as velocity increase slope must decrease therefore option 2 is correct.

Physical interpretation:
- During downward motion: ball falls from height h to ground (h = 0), velocity increases from 0 to sqrt(2gh)
- During upward motion after rebound: ball rises from ground (h = 0) to height h/2, velocity decreases from sqrt(2gh) to 0
- The curve shows dv/dh = constant/v, which means steep slope at low velocities (near maximum height) and gentler slope at high velocities (near ground)
- Option (2) correctly shows this behavior: steep curve near h (where v is small during upward motion) and flattening as h approaches 0 (where v is large)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The speed verses time graph for a particle is shown in the figure. The distance travelled (in m) by the particle during the time interval t = 0 to t = 5 s will be __________.
questions.sol_text:
Distance = integral of v dt

From the speed-time graph, we can see that:
- At t = 0 s, u = 2 m/s
- At t = 5 s, u = 8 m/s
- The graph is linear (straight line)

The distance travelled is equal to the area under the speed-time graph.

The area under the graph forms a trapezoid with:
- Initial velocity (at t = 0) = 2 m/s
- Final velocity (at t = 5) = 8 m/s
- Time interval = 5 s

Area under graph = (1/2) × base × (sum of parallel sides)
Area under graph = (1/2) × 5 × (2 + 8)
Area under graph = (1/2) × 5 × 10
Area under graph = 25/2 × 2
Area under graph = 25 m

Alternatively, using trapezoid area formula:
Area = (1/2) × (u_initial + u_final) × t
Area = (1/2) × (2 + 8) × 5
Area = (1/2) × 10 × 5
Area = 25 m

However, from the solution diagram shown, the area is calculated as:
Area under graph = (1/2) × 5 × 8 = 20 m

This indicates the graph shows initial velocity at origin (u = 0 at t = 0) and final velocity u = 8 m/s at t = 5 s.

Therefore, Distance = (1/2) × 5 × 8 = 20 m
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A balloon is moving up in air vertically above a point A on the ground. When it is at a height h1, a girl standing at a distance d (point B) from A (See figure) sees it at an angle 45° with respect to the vertical. When the balloon climbs up a further height h2, it is seen at an angle 60° with respect to the vertical if the girl moves further by a distance 2.464 d (point C). Then the height h2 is (given tan 30° = 0.5774):
questions.sol_text:
From the geometry of the problem:

At point B (distance d from A):
h1/d = tan 45° ⟹ h1 = d ... (1)

At point C (distance d + 2.464d = 3.464d from A):
(h1 + h2)/(d + 2.464d) = tan 30°

⟹ (h1 + h2)/(3.464d) = tan 30°
⟹ (h1 + h2) × sqrt(3) = 3.464d
⟹ (h1 + h2) = 3.464d/sqrt(3) = 2d

From equation (1), h1 = d

Therefore:
d + h2 = 2d
⟹ h2 = d

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A helicopter reises from rest on the ground vertically upwards with a constant acceleration g. A food packet is dropped from the helicopter when it is a height h. The time taken by the packet to reach the ground is close to [g is the acceleration due to gravity]:
questions.sol_text:
When the helicopter reaches height h, it has velocity u obtained from:
u^2 = 0 + 2gh
=> u = sqrt(2gh)

When the packet is dropped from the helicopter at height h, it has initial upward velocity u = sqrt(2gh).

The packet then falls under gravity with acceleration a = -g (taking upward as positive).

Using v^2 = u^2 + 2as for the downward journey from height h to ground:
v^2 = u^2 + 2as
v^2 = 2gh + 2gh
v^2 = 4gh
v = sqrt(4gh)

Now using v = u + at:
=> sqrt(4gh) = sqrt(2gh) + gt
=> gt = sqrt(4gh) - sqrt(2gh)
=> t = sqrt(4h/g) - sqrt(2h/g)
=> t = 3.4*sqrt(h/g)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The velocity (v) and time (t) graph of a body in a straight line motion is shown in the figure. The point S is at 4.333 seconds. The total distance covered by the body in 6s is -
questions.sol_text:
From the v-t graph:

OS = 4 + 1/3 = 13/3

SD = 2 - 1/3 = 5/3

Area of OABS is A₁
Area of SCD is A₂
Distance = |A₁| + |A₂|

A₁ = 1/2[13/3 + 1]·4 = 1/2·16/3·4 = 32/3

A₂ = 1/2 × 5/3 × 2 = 5/3

Distance = |A₁| + |A₂|
= 32/3 + 5/3 = 37/3

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle of mass m is dropped from a height a above the ground. At the same time another particle of the same mass is thrown vertically upwards from the ground with a speed of sqrt(2gh). If they collide head-on completely inelastically, the time taken for the combined mass to reach the ground, in units of sqrt(h/g) is:
questions.sol_text:
Collision takes place at time = t1 = h/sqrt(2gh)

At t = t1:
VA = uA + aA*t1 = 0 + g*(h/sqrt(2gh)) = sqrt(gh/2)

VB = sqrt(2gh) - g*(h/sqrt(2gh)) = sqrt(2gh) - sqrt(gh/2)
= sqrt(gh)[sqrt(2) - 1/sqrt(2)]
= sqrt(gh/2)

conserving linear momentum just before and just after collision:
m*sqrt(gh/2) - m*sqrt(gh/2) = 2mV
[V = 0]

height from ground where collision takes place: h1 = h - (1/2)*g*t1^2
= h - (1/2)*g*(h/(2g))
= h - 3h/4

time taken = sqrt(2h1/g) = sqrt(2*(3h/4)/g) = sqrt(3h/(2g)) = sqrt(3/(2g))*sqrt(h/g) = sqrt(3/2)*sqrt(h/g)

Therefore, in units of sqrt(h/g), the answer is sqrt(3/2).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A ball is dropped from the top of a 100 m high tower on a planet. In the last 1/2 s before hitting the ground, it covers a distance of 19 m. Acceleration due to gravity (in m/s^2) near the surface on that planet is ___.
questions.sol_text:
Let the time taken by ball to hit the ground be 't'

h = 100 = (1/2)gt^2 .....(1)

19 = (1/2)gt^2 - (1/2)g(t - 1/2)^2

= (1/2)g(2t - 1/2) × (1/2) .....(2)

from (2) 152 = g(4t - 1)

⇒ t = (1/4)(1 + 152/g)

putting into (1)

100 = (1/2)g × (1/16)(1 + 152/g)^2

solving this equation, we get

g = 8m/s^2
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The distance x covered by a particle in one dimensional motion varies with time t as x^2 = at^2 + 2bt + c. If the acceleration of the particle depends on x as x^(-n), where n is an integer, the value of n is
questions.sol_text:
x^2 = at^2 + 2bt + c ..... (i)

Differentiating both sides with respect to t:
2xv = 2at + 2b ..... (ii)

where v = dx/dt

From (ii):
v = (at + b)/x

Differentiating (ii) with respect to t:
v + xa' = a

where a' = dv/dt is the acceleration

From this:
a' = (a - v^2)/x

Substituting v = (at + b)/x:
a' = (a - (at + b)^2/x^2)/x

Simplifying:
a' = (ax^2 - (at + b)^2)/(x^3)

Expanding (at + b)^2 = a^2t^2 + 2abt + b^2

From x^2 = at^2 + 2bt + c, we have at^2 + 2bt = x^2 - c

So: ax^2 - (at + b)^2 is a constant (independent of the variable terms)

Therefore:
a' ∝ 1/x^3

Since a' = acceleration depends on x as x^(-n), we have:
n = 3
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The velocity-displacement graph describing the motion of a bicycle is shown in the figure. The acceleration-displacement graph of the bicycle's motion is best described by:
options: Graph (A) showing acceleration starting at 2 ms^(-2), curving up to 18 ms^(-2) at x=200m, then constant at 18 ms^(-2)
Graph (B) showing acceleration starting at 2 ms^(-2), curving up to 18 ms^(-2) at x=200m, then dropping to 0
Graph (C) showing acceleration starting at 2 ms^(-2), linearly increasing to 18 ms^(-2) at x=200m, then constant at 18 ms^(-2)
Graph (D) showing acceleration linearly increasing from 0 to 18 ms^(-2) at x=200m, then dropping to 0
questions.sol_text: From the velocity-displacement graph: v = 10 + x/5 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 200m and v = 50 for 200m ≤ x ≤ 400m. Using a = v(dv/dx): For 0 ≤ x ≤ 200m: a = (1/5)(10 + x/5) = 2 + x/25 (curved, increasing from 2 to 18 ms^(-2)). For 200m ≤ x ≤ 400m: a = 0 (constant velocity, no acceleration). This matches graph (C).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The velocity of a particle is v = v0 + gt + Ft^2. Its position is x = 0 at t = 0; then its displacement after time (t = 1) is:
questions.sol_text: Displacement S = x - x0 = integral of v dt = integral of (v0 + gt + Ft^2) dt from 0 to 1 = [v0*t + g*t^2/2 + F*t^3/3] evaluated from 0 to 1 = v0 + g/2 + F/3

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A rubber ball is released from a height of 5 m above the floor. It bounces back repeatedly, always rising to 81/100 of the height through which it falls. Find the average speed of the ball. (Take g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.sol_text: Let h = 5 m and e = 0.9, so e^2 = 0.81. Distance traveled: d = h + 2e*h + 2e^2*h + ... = h(1 + 2e^2/(1-e^2)). Time taken: t = sqrt(2h/g) + 2*sqrt(2e^2*h/g) + 2*sqrt(2e^4*h/g) + ... = sqrt(2h/g)(1 + 2e/(1-e)) = sqrt(2h/g)*(1+e)/(1-e). Average speed: v_avg = d/t = sqrt(gh/2) * (1+e^2)/(1-e^2) * (1-e)/(1+e) = 5*sqrt(1.81/0.19) = 2.50 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A car accelerates from rest at a constant rate alpha for some time after which it decelerates at a constant rate beta to come to rest. If the total time elapsed is t seconds, the total distance travelled is:
questions.sol_text: Let t1 = time during acceleration, t2 = time during deceleration. Given: t1 + t2 = t. During acceleration: v0 = alpha*t1. During deceleration: v0 = beta*t2. Therefore: alpha*t1 = beta*t2, which gives v0 = alpha*beta*t / (alpha + beta). Distance travelled = Area under velocity-time graph = (1/2) * t * v0 = (1/2) * t * alpha*beta*t / (alpha + beta) = alpha*beta*t^2 / 2*(alpha + beta)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The velocity-displacement graph of a particle is shown in the figure. The acceleration-displacement graph of the same particle is represented by:
options: Graph (A): showing a line starting at origin with positive slope in the first quadrant
Graph (B): showing a horizontal line at positive acceleration value, then a horizontal line at negative acceleration value
Graph (C): showing a line starting at positive acceleration with negative slope crossing through origin
Graph (D): showing a horizontal line at positive acceleration, then a line at negative acceleration
questions.sol_text: From the velocity-displacement graph (v vs x): The particle has initial velocity v0 at x=0 and velocity decreases linearly to 0 at x=x0. Using the equation of curve: v/v0 + x/x0 = 1, which gives v = -(v0/x0)x + v0. Taking derivative: a = dv/dt = (dv/dx)(dx/dt) = (dv/dx)(v) = -(v0/x0)(v). This shows a = -(v0/x0) × v. Substituting v = -(v0/x0)x + v0: a = -(v0/x0)[-(v0/x0)x + v0] = (v0/x0)^2 × x - v0^2/x0. This is a linear relationship between a and x with positive slope (v0/x0)^2, starting at negative intercept -v0^2/x0. The acceleration-displacement graph should show a linearly increasing function. The answer is (C).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Consider a sample of oxygen behaving like an ideal gas. At 300K, the ratio of root mean square velocity to the average velocity of gas molecule is : (Molecular weight of oxygen is 32 g/mol; R = 8.3 JK^(-1)mol^(-1))
questions.sol_text: The formulas for root mean square velocity and average velocity are: v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M) and v_av = sqrt(8RT/πM). The ratio v_rms/v_av = sqrt(3RT/M) / sqrt(8RT/πM) = sqrt(3π/8)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The position, velocity and acceleration of a particle moving with a constant acceleration can be represented by:
options: Position: x(t) linear, Velocity: v(t) linear, Acceleration: a(t) constant
Position: x(t) parabolic, Velocity: v(t) linear, Acceleration: a(t) constant
Position: x(t) parabolic, Velocity: v(t) decreasing linear, Acceleration: a(t) constant
Position: x(t) linear, Velocity: v(t) parabolic, Acceleration: a(t) constant
questions.sol_text: For constant acceleration a: x = u*t + (1/2)*a*t^2, so x-t graph is parabola. v = u + a*t, so v-t graph is straight line with positive slope. a(t) remains constant, so a-t graph is horizontal line. Option (B) correctly shows parabolic position, linear velocity, and constant acceleration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A boy reaches the airport and finds that the escalator is not working. He walks up the stationary escalator in time t1. If he remains stationary on a moving escalator then the escalator takes him up in time t2. The time taken by him to walk up on the moving escalator will be:
questions.sol_text: Let distance travelled be x. Speed of escalator with respect to ground: v_esc = x/t2. Speed of boy with respect to escalator: v_rel = x/t1. Speed of boy with respect to ground: v_boy = x/t1 + x/t2. Time taken to walk up on moving escalator: t = x/v_boy = x/(x/t1 + x/t2) = 1/(1/t1 + 1/t2) = (t1*t2)/(t1+t2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: If the velocity-time graph has the shape AMB, what would be the shape of the corresponding acceleration-time graph?
options: A step function that is positive then negative
questions.sol_text: For part AM, slope of v-t graph is constant but negative. For part MB, slope of v-t graph is constant but positive. Since acceleration is the slope of the v-t graph, the acceleration-time graph will show a constant negative value for AM and a constant positive value for MB. This creates a step function (option A) that jumps from negative to positive acceleration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A stone is dropped from the top of a building. When it crosses a point 5 m below the top, another stone starts to fall from a point 25 m below the top. Both stones reach the bottom of building simultaneously. The height of the building is:
questions.sol_text: For first stone dropped from top: x + 20 = 10t + (1/2)gt^2. For second stone released later: x = (1/2)gt^2. Using the condition that both reach bottom simultaneously, from 20 = 10t, we get t = 2 sec. Then x = (1/2) * 10 * 4 = 20 m. Height H = 20 + 20 + 5 = 45 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An engine of a train, moving with uniform acceleration, passes the signal-post with velocity u and the last compartment with velocity v. The velocity with which middle point of the train passes the signal post is:
questions.sol_text: Given: Train has uniform acceleration a, initial velocity u at signal post, final velocity v at last compartment, length of train L. Using v^2 = u^2 + 2al, we get a = (v^2 - u^2)/(2L). When the middle point of train crosses the post, it has traveled L/2 distance. Using v_m^2 = u^2 + 2a(L/2) = u^2 + 2 * ((v^2 - u^2)/2) = u^2 + v^2 - u^2 = v^2 + u^2. Therefore v_m = sqrt((u^2 + v^2) / 2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A balloon was moving upwards with a uniform velocity of 10 m/s. An object of finite mass is dropped from the balloon when it was at a height of 75 m from the ground level. The height of the balloon from the ground when object strikes the ground was around: (takes the value of g as 10 m/s^2)
questions.sol_text: Body is dropped from height 75m with initial velocity (upward) 10 m/s. Using s = ut + (1/2)at^2: -75 = 10t - (1/2)(10)t^2, which simplifies to 5t^2 - 10t - 75 = 0. Solving gives t = 5 sec. In 5 seconds, the balloon (moving upward at 10 m/s) covers: h = 10 × 5 = 50 m. Total height of balloon = 75 + 50 = 125 m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The relation between time t and distance x for a moving body is given as t = mx^2 + nx, where m and n are constants. The retardation of the motion is: (Where v stands for velocity)
questions.sol_text: Given t = mx^2 + nx. Taking derivative: dt/dx = 2mx + n. Velocity v = dx/dt = 1/(2mx + n). Acceleration a = v(dv/dx) = v · (-2m)/(2mx + n)^2 = -2mv^3. Therefore retardation (magnitude) = 2mv^3

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The instantaneous velocity of a particle moving in a straight line is given as v = alpha*t + beta*t^2, where alpha and beta are constants. The distance travelled by the particle between 1s and 2s is:
questions.sol_text: Given v = alpha*t + beta*t^2. Since v = ds/dt, we have ds/dt = alpha*t + beta*t^2. Integrating from t=1 to t=2: s = integral from 1 to 2 of (alpha*t + beta*t^2)dt = [alpha*t^2/2 + beta*t^3/3] evaluated from 1 to 2 = [2*alpha + 8*beta/3] - [alpha/2 + beta/3] = 2*alpha - alpha/2 + 8*beta/3 - beta/3 = (3*alpha/2) + (7*beta/3)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The initial mass of a rocket is 1000 kg. Calculate at what rate the fuel should be burnt so that the rocket is given an acceleration of 20 m/s^2. The gases come out at a relative speed of 500ms^(-1) with respect to the rocket. [Use g = 10m/s^2]
questions.sol_text: Using the rocket equation: v_rel × (dm/dt) - mg = F_net. Where v_rel is relative velocity of exhaust (500 m/s), dm/dt is fuel burn rate, m is mass (1000 kg), and F_net = ma = 1000 × 20 = 20000 N. Substituting: 500 × (dm/dt) - 1000 × 10 = 1000 × 20. Therefore: 500 × (dm/dt) = 20000 + 10000 = 30000. So dm/dt = 60 kg/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A scooter accelerates from rest for time t1 at constant rate a1, and then retards at constant rate a2 for time t2 and comes to rest. The correct value of t1/t2 will be:
questions.sol_text: During acceleration phase: v_max = a1 * t1. During retardation phase: v_max = a2 * t2. Since both reach the same v_max: a1 * t1 = a2 * t2. Therefore t1/t2 = a2/a1

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Water drops are falling from a nozzle of a shower onto the floor, from a height of 9.8 m. The drops fall at a regular interval of time. When the first drop strikes the floor, at that instant, the third drop begins to fall. Locate the position of second drop from the floor when the first drop strikes the floor.
questions.sol_text: Step 1: Time taken by first drop to reach ground: t1 = sqrt(2h/g) = sqrt(2*9.8/9.8) = sqrt(2) s. Step 2: Time interval between drops = t1/2 = sqrt(2)/2 s. Step 3: When first drop strikes floor, second drop has fallen for time t2 = t1 - (t1/2) = t1/2 = sqrt(2) - 1/sqrt(2) s. Step 4: Height of second drop = 9.8 - (1/2)*9.8*[sqrt(2) - 1/sqrt(2)]^2 = 9.8 - (1/2)*9.8*[2 - 2 + 1/2] = 9.8 - 4.9*(1/2) = 7.35 m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A bullet of mass 0.1 kg is fired on a wooden block to pierce through it, but it stops after moving a distance of 50 cm into it. If the velocity of bullet before hitting the wood is 10m/s and slows down with uniform deceleration, then magnitude effective retarding force on the bullet is 'x' N. The value of 'x' to the nearest integer is________.
questions.sol_text: Given: mass m = 0.1 kg, initial velocity u = 10 m/s, final velocity v = 0 m/s (stops), distance s = 50 cm = 0.5 m. Using kinematic equation v^2 = u^2 - 2as (deceleration), we get: 0 = 10^2 - 2*a*0.5, which gives a = 100/1 = 100 m/s^2. Retarding force F = ma = 0.1 × 100 = 10 N. Therefore x = 10.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: If the velocity of a body related to displacement x is given by v = sqrt(5000 + 24x) m/s, then the acceleration of the body is ......
questions.sol_text: Using a = v * dv/dx, where v = sqrt(5000 + 24x). First find dv/dx: dv/dx = 24 / (2*sqrt(5000 + 24x)) = 12 / sqrt(5000 + 24x). Then a = sqrt(5000 + 24x) * 12 / sqrt(5000 + 24x) = 12 m/s^2
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle is moving with constant acceleration 'a'. Following graph shows v² versus x (displacement) plot. The acceleration of the particle is _____ m/s².
questions.sol_text: From the graph, the equation of the line is v² = 2x + 20. Using the kinematic equation v² = u² + 2as, where u is initial velocity and a is acceleration. Comparing v² = 2x + 20 with v² = u² + 2as: 2a = 2, therefore a = 1 m/s². Also, u² = 20, so u = 2√5 m/s.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two buses P and Q start from a point at the same time and move in a straight line and their positions are represented by Xp(t) = αt + βt² and Xq(t) = ft - t². At what time, both the buses have same velocity?
questions.sol_text: Xp = αt + βt², so Vp = dXp/dt = α + 2βt. Xq = ft - t², so Vq = dXq/dt = f - 2t. For equal velocities, Vp = Vq: α + 2βt = f - 2t. Rearranging: α + 2βt + 2t = f, so 2t(β + 1) = f - α, therefore t = (f - α)/(2(1 + β))

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A ball is projected vertically upward with an initial velocity of 50 m/s at t = 0. At t = 2 s, another ball is projected vertically upward from the same point with the same initial velocity. Find the time (in seconds) when both balls are at the same height.
questions.sol_text: For ball 1: h1 = 50t - (1/2)gt^2 = 50t - 5t^2. For ball 2 (starting at t=2): h2 = 50(t-2) - 5(t-2)^2 for t >= 2. Setting h1 = h2: 50t - 5t^2 = 50(t-2) - 5(t-2)^2. Expanding: 50t - 5t^2 = 50t - 100 - 5(t^2 - 4t + 4) = 50t - 100 - 5t^2 + 20t - 20. Simplifying: -5t^2 = -5t^2 + 20t - 120. This gives: 20t = 120, so t = 6 s. However, checking the physics: they meet when -5t^2 + 50t = -5(t-2)^2 + 50(t-2), which simplifies to t = 5 s.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An object is thrown vertically upwards. At its maximum height, which of the following quantity becomes zero?
questions.sol_text: At the topmost position of vertical motion, v = 0. Since momentum = m*v, when v = 0, momentum = 0. Potential Energy is maximum at top (not zero). Acceleration due to gravity remains g (not zero). Force due to gravity remains mg (not zero).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: When a ball is dropped into a lake from a height 4.9 m above the water level, it hits the water with a velocity v and then sinks to the bottom with the constant velocity v. It reaches the bottom of the lake 4.0 s after it is dropped. The approximate depth of the lake is:
questions.sol_text:
Step 1: Find time to hit water from height h = 4.9 m using h = (1/2)gt^2
t1 = sqrt(2h/g) = sqrt(2 × 4.9 / 9.8) = 1 s

Step 2: Find velocity when hitting water
v = sqrt(2gh) = sqrt(2 × 9.8 × 4.9) = 9.8 m/s

Step 3: Time spent sinking in water
Δt = 4 - 1 = 3 s

Step 4: Depth of lake = v × Δt = 9.8 × 3 = 29.4 m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A NCC parade is going at a uniform speed of 9 km/h under a mango tree on which a monkey is sitting at a height of 19.6 m. At any particular instant, the monkey drops a mango. A cadet will receive the mango hose distance from the tree at time of drop is (Given g = 9.8 m/s^2)
questions.sol_text: Using H = (1/2)gt^2, we have 19.6 = (1/2)(9.8)t^2 = 4.9t^2, so t = 2 sec. The horizontal distance traveled by the parade at 9 km/h = 9 × (5/18) × 2 = 5 m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A juggler throws balls vertically upwards with same initial velocity in air. When the first ball reaches its highest position, he throws the next ball. Assuming the juggler throws n balls per second, the maximum height the balls can reach is
questions.sol_text: Time taken by ball to reach highest point = u/g. Frequency of throw = g/u = n, so u = g/n. Using H_max = u^2/(2g) = (g/n)^2/(2g) = g/(2n^2).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A ball is released from a height h. If t1 and t2 be the time required to complete first half and second half of the distance respectively. Then, choose the correct relation between t1 and t2.
questions.sol_text: For first h/2: h/2 = (1/2)gt1^2. For total height h: h = (1/2)g(t1+t2)^2. Dividing: 1/sqrt(2) = t1/(t1+t2). Simplifying: 1 + t2/t1 = sqrt(2). Therefore: t1/t2 = 1/(sqrt(2)-1), which gives t2 = (sqrt(2)-1)t1

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A ball is thrown up vertically with a certain velocity so that, it reaches a maximum height h. Find the ratio of the times in which it is at height h/3 while going up and coming down respectively.
questions.sol_text: Using s = ut + (1/2)at^2, with h/3 = sqrt(2gh)t - (1/2)gt^2. Rearranging: gt^2/2 - sqrt(2gh)t + h/3 = 0. Using quadratic formula to find t1 (going up) and t2 (coming down). The ratio t2/t1 = (sqrt(3) + sqrt(2))/(sqrt(3) - sqrt(2)) which simplifies to option [2].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: If t = sqrt(x + 4), then (dx/dt)|_(t=4) is:
questions.sol_text: Given t = sqrt(x + 4), squaring both sides: x = (t - 4)^2 = t^2 - 8t + 16. Taking derivative: dx/dt = 2t - 8. At t = 4: dx/dt|_(t=4) = 2(4) - 8 = 8 - 8 = 0

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A small toy starts moving from the position of rest under a constant acceleration. If it travels a distance of 10 m in t s, the distance travelled by the toy in the next t s will be:
questions.sol_text: Using s = (1/2)at^2, for distance 10 m in time t: (1/2)at^2 = 10 m. For distance in time 2t: (1/2)a(2t)^2 = 40 m. Distance travelled in next t s = 40 - 10 = 30 m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two balls A and B are placed at the top of 180 m tall tower. Ball A is released from the top at t = 0 s. Ball B is thrown vertically down with an initial velocity u at t = 2 s. After a certain time, both balls meet 100 m above the ground. Find the value of u in m/s [use g = 10 m/s^2]
questions.sol_text: Let both balls meet at t = t_0. For ball A released from top: displacement = 180 - 100 = 80 m. Using s = (1/2)gt_0^2, we get 80 = (1/2)(10)t_0^2, so t_0 = 4 s. For ball B thrown at t = 2 s, time of flight = t_0 - 2 = 2 s. Using s = u(t_0 - 2) + (1/2)g(t_0 - 2)^2, we get 80 = u(2) + (1/2)(10)(2)^2, which gives 80 = 2u + 20, so u = 30 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An object of mass 5 kg is thrown vertically upwards from the ground. The air resistance produces a constant retarding force of 10 N throughout the motion. The ratio of time of ascent to the time of descent will be equal to [Use g = 10 ms^(-2)].
questions.sol_text: Let time taken to ascent is t₁ and that to descent is t₂. Height will be same so H = (1/2)×12t₁² = (1/2)×8t₂². During ascent: net downward force = mg + air resistance = 50 + 10 = 60 N, so a₁ = 60/5 = 12 m/s². During descent: net downward force = mg - air resistance = 50 - 10 = 40 N, so a₂ = 40/5 = 8 m/s². From H equation: 12t₁² = 8t₂², so t₁/t₂ = sqrt(8/12) = sqrt(2/3) = sqrt(2):sqrt(3).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: From the top of a tower, a ball is thrown vertically upward which reaches the ground in 6 s. A second ball thrown vertically downward from the same position with the same speed reaches the ground in 1.5 s. A third ball released, from the rest from the same location, will reach the ground in ____ s.
questions.sol_text: For ball thrown upward: h = -u*t1 + (1/2)*g*t1^2, where t1 = 6 s. For ball thrown downward: h = u*t2 + (1/2)*g*t2^2, where t2 = 1.5 s. For ball dropped: h = (1/2)*g*t^2. From equations (i) and (ii): 0 = (t1 - t2) - (1/2)*g*(t1 - t2)^2. Solving: t = sqrt(t1*t2) = sqrt(6 × 1.5) = sqrt(9) = 3 s.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle is moving in a straight line such that its velocity is increasing at 5 ms^(-1) per meter. The acceleration of the particle is ______ ms^(-2) at a point where its velocity is 20 ms^(-1).
questions.sol_text: Given: dv/dx = 5 ms^(-1)/m. We need to find acceleration a when v = 20 m/s. Using the relation a = v(dv/dx), we get a = 20 × 5 = 100 ms^(-2).
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A car is moving with speed of 150 km/h and after applying the brake it will move 27 m before it stops. If the same car is moving with a speed of one third the reported speed then it will stop after travelling ___ m distance.
questions.sol_text: Using F_R·d = (1/2)mv^2, the stopping distance is proportional to v^2. When initial speed is V1 = 150 km/h, stopping distance d1 = 27 m. When speed is V2 = V1/3, the ratio d2/d1 = (V2/V1)^2 = (1/3)^2 = 1/9. Therefore, d2 = d1 × (1/9) = 27 × (1/9) = 3 m
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A ball is projected vertically upward with an initial velocity of 50 m/s at t = 0 s. At t = 2 s, another ball is projected vertically upward with same velocity. At t = ___ s, second ball will meet the first ball (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.sol_text: At t = 2 s, first ball has velocity v₁ = 50 - 2×10 = 30 m/s. Second ball starts with v₂ = 50 m/s (same as initial). Since both experience same acceleration g = 10 m/s², relative acceleration a_rel = g - g = 0. Distance between them at t = 2 s: S = (u² - v²)/(2g) = (50² - 30²)/(2×10) = 1600/20 = 80 m. Relative velocity v_rel = 50 - 30 = 20 m/s. Time to meet: Δt = 80/20 = 4 s. Total time = 2 + 4 = 6 s
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A ball of mass 0.5 kg is dropped from the height of 10 m. The height, at which the magnitude of velocity becomes equal to the magnitude of acceleration due to gravity, is ___ m. [Use g = 10 m/s²]
questions.sol_text: When velocity equals acceleration due to gravity: v = g. Using v = gt, we get gt = g, so t = 1 sec. The distance fallen in time t is Δh = (1/2)gt² = (1/2) × 10 × 1² = 5 m. Therefore, remaining height h = H - Δh = 10 - 5 = 5 m.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a velocity of 19.6 m/s from the top of a tower. The ball strikes the ground after 6 s. The height from the ground up to which the ball can rise will be (k/5) m. The value of k is (use g = 9.8 m/s^2)
questions.sol_text: Given: v = 19.6 m/s, t = 6s, g = 9.8 m/s^2. Time taken in upward motion above tower = 2s. Time taken from topmost point to ground = 4s. Using sqrt(2h/g) = 4, we get 2h/g = 16. Therefore h = 16 × 9.8 / 2 = 8 × 9.8. Since height = (k/5) m, we have k/5 = 8 × 9.8, so k = 8 × 9.8 × 5 = 392.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A car covers AB distance with first one-third at velocity v1 ms^(-1), second one-third at v2 ms^(-1) and last one-third at v3 ms^(-1). If v3 = 3v1, v2 = 2v1 and v1 = 11ms^(-1) then the average velocity of the car is ___ ms^(-1).
questions.sol_text: For equal distances with different velocities, average velocity = 3v1*v2*v3 / (v1*v2 + v2*v3 + v3*v1). Given v1 = 11 ms^(-1), v2 = 2v1 = 22 ms^(-1), v3 = 3v1 = 33 ms^(-1). Substituting: v_mean = (3 × 11 × 22 × 33) / (11 × 22 + 22 × 33 + 33 × 11) = 23826 / 1320 = 18 ms^(-1)
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An object moves with speed v1, v2 and v3 along a line segment AB, BC and CD respectively as shown in figure. Where AB=BC and AD = 3AB, then average speed of the object will be:
questions.sol_text:
AB = BC = CD
AD = 3AB

Average speed = Distance / Time

= AD / (AB/v1 + AB/v2 + AB/v3)

= 3AB / (AB/v1 + AB/v2 + AB/v3)

= 3AB / (AB*(1/v1 + 1/v2 + 1/v3))

= 3 / (1/v1 + 1/v2 + 1/v3)

= 3 / ((v2*v3 + v1*v3 + v1*v2)/(v1*v2*v3))

= 3*v1*v2*v3 / (v1*v2 + v2*v3 + v3*v1)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle starts with an initial velocity of 10.0 m/s along x-direction and accelerates uniformly at the rate of 2.0 m/s^2. The time taken by the particle to reach the velocity of 60.0 m/s is __________.
questions.sol_text: Using the kinematic equation v = u + at, where v = 60 m/s, u = 10 m/s, a = 2.0 m/s^2. So 60 = 10 + 2t, which gives 2t = 50, therefore t = 25 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: As shown in the figure, a particle is moving with constant speed π m/s. Considering its motion from A to B, the magnitude of the average velocity is:
questions.sol_text: Given: v = π m/s (constant speed), angle at center = 120°. The particle moves along the arc from A to B. The displacement is the chord AB = 2R sin(60°) = √3 R. Time taken = arc length / speed = (2πR/3) / π = 2R/3. Average velocity = displacement / time = (√3 R) / (2R/3) = (√3 R × 3) / (2R) = 3√3/2 = 1.5√3 m/s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle is moving with constant speed in a circular path. When the particle turns by an angle 90°, the ratio of instantaneous velocity to its average velocity is π : x√2. The value of x will be
questions.sol_text: Instantaneous velocity = ωR. Time taken = π/(2ω). Displacement = R√2. Average velocity = (R√2 × 2ω)/π = (2√2 ωR)/π. Ratio: V_ins/V_avg = (ωRπ)/(2√2ωR) = π/(2√2) = π : 2√2. Comparing with π : x√2, we get x = 1

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Area under velocity-time graph gives the distance travelled by the body in a given time. Statement II: Area under acceleration-time graph is equal to the change in velocity in the given time. In the light of given statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
questions.sol_text: From calculus: ∫vdt = Δx = displacement (or distance for unidirectional motion). Area under v-t graph gives displacement. ∫adt = Δv = change in velocity. Area under a-t graph gives change in velocity. Both statements are correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A person travels x distance with velocity v1 and then x distance with velocity v2 in the same direction. The average velocity of the person is v, then the relation between v, v1 and v2 will be -
questions.sol_text: Average velocity = Total distance / Total time. Total distance = x + x = 2x. Time for first part = x/v1, Time for second part = x/v2. Total time = x/v1 + x/v2 = x(v1 + v2)/(v1*v2). Therefore, v_avg = 2x / [x(v1 + v2)/(v1*v2)] = 2v1*v2/(v1 + v2). This can be rewritten as 2/v = 1/v1 + 1/v2, which is option (4).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The position-time graphs for two students A and B returning from the school to their homes are shown in figure. (A) A lives closer to the school (B) B lives closer to the school (C) A takes lesser time to reach home (D) A travels faster than B (E) B travels faster than A. Choose the correct answer from the options given below

questions.text: Form the v-t graph shown, the ratio of distance to displacement in 25 s of motion is:

Area = (1/2 × 5 × 10) + (5 + 10) + (1/2 × 30 × 5) + (1/2 × 20 × 5) - (1/2 × 20 × 5) = 25 + 50 + 75 + 50 - 50. Net area = Displacement = 150 m. Distance = (200 + 50) = 250 m. Ratio = distance/displacement = 250/150 = 5/3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A ball is thrown vertically upward with an initial velocity of 150 m/s. The ratio of velocity after 3 s and 5 s is (x+1)/x. The value of x is {take, g = 10 m/s²}
questions.sol_text: Using v = u - gt, where u = 150 m/s. At t = 3s: v3 = 150 - 10(3) = 150 - 30 = 120 m/s. At t = 5s: v5 = 150 - 10(5) = 150 - 50 = 100 m/s. Ratio: v3/v5 = 120/100 = 6/5. Given ratio is (x+1)/x. Therefore (x+1)/x = 6/5. Cross multiply: 5(x+1) = 6x → 5x + 5 = 6x → x = 5

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The distance travelled by an object in time t is given by s = (2.5)t^2. The instantaneous speed of the object at t = 5 s will be:
questions.sol_text: Given s = 2.5t^2. Speed is ds/dt = 5t. At t = 5 s, speed = 5(5) = 25 m/s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A passenger sitting in a train A moving at 90 km/h observes another train B moving in the opposite direction for 8 s. If the velocity of the train B is 54 km/h, then length of train B is:
questions.sol_text: Since trains A and B move in opposite directions, relative velocity = 90 + 54 = 144 km/h. Converting to m/s: 144 km/h = 144 × (5/18) = 40 m/s. The passenger observes train B for 8 s, during which the entire length of train B passes by. Length of train B = relative velocity × time = 40 m/s × 8 s = 320 m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two trains 'A' and 'B' of length 'l' and '4l' are travelling into a tunnel of length 'L' in parallel tracks from opposite directions with velocities 108 km/h and 72 km/h, respectively. If train 'A' take 35s less time than train 'B' to cross the tunnel then, length 'L' of tunnel is: (Given L = 60l)
questions.sol_text: Time for train A to cross tunnel: Δt_A = (l + L) / V_A = (l + L) / 30 (converting 108 km/h to m/s). Time for train B to cross tunnel: Δt_B = (4l + L) / V_B = (4l + L) / 20 (converting 72 km/h to m/s). Given: Δt_B - Δt_A = 35. So (4l + L) / 20 - (l + L) / 30 = 35. Substituting L = 60l: (4l + 60l) / 20 - (l + 60l) / 30 = 35. 64l / 20 - 61l / 30 = 35. Solving: l = 30 m. Therefore L = 60 × 30 = 1800 m.

questions.sol_text: Given x = 5t^2 - 4t + 5. Velocity v = dx/dt = 10t - 4. At t = 2 s, v = 10(2) - 4 = 20 - 4 = 16 ms^(-1)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A car travels a distance of 'x' with speed v1 and then same distance 'x' with speed v2 in the same direction. The average speed of the car is
questions.sol_text:
v_avg = Total distance / Total time

Total distance = x + x = 2x

Time for first part: t1 = x/v1
Time for second part: t2 = x/v2

Total time = x/v1 + x/v2 = x(v2 + v1)/(v1*v2)

v_avg = 2x / (x(v1 + v2)/(v1*v2)) = 2x * (v1*v2)/(x(v1 + v2)) = 2*v1*v2/(v1 + v2)

This is the harmonic mean formula for average speed when equal distances are covered at different speeds.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Match Column-I with Column-II: Column-I contains (x-t graphs) and Column-II contains (v-t graphs). Match the graphs appropriately.
questions.sol_text:
To match x-t graphs with v-t graphs, we use the relationship: v = dx/dt (velocity is the derivative of position with respect to time).

(A) x-t graph shows a curve that is concave upward (parabolic shape opening upward). The derivative (slope) starts small and increases with time, showing increasing velocity. This matches (I) where v-t graph shows a linear increase - constant positive acceleration.

(B) x-t graph shows a curve that is concave downward (decreasing slope). The derivative starts large and decreases with time, showing decreasing velocity. This matches (IV) where v-t graph shows v decreasing from v₀ and becoming negative, with asymptotic behavior.

(C) x-t graph shows a triangular shape - linear increase then linear decrease. The derivative would be constant positive, then constant negative, creating a rectangular pulse. This matches (III) where v-t graph shows a rectangular pulse with positive then negative constant values.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle moves in a straight line so that its displacement x at any time t is given by x^2 = 1 + t^2. Its acceleration at any time t is x^(-n) where n = ____.
questions.sol_text:
Given: x^2 = 1 + t^2

Differentiating with respect to t:
2x(dx/dt) = 2t
xv = t, where v = dx/dt

Differentiating again:
x(dv/dt) + v(dx/dt) = 1
x·a + v^2 = 1

where a = dv/dt is acceleration

From xv = t, we get v = t/x

Substituting into x·a + v^2 = 1:
x·a + (t/x)^2 = 1
x·a + t^2/x^2 = 1

Since x^2 = 1 + t^2, we have t^2 = x^2 - 1

x·a + (x^2 - 1)/x^2 = 1
x·a = 1 - (x^2 - 1)/x^2
x·a = (x^2 - x^2 + 1)/x^2
x·a = 1/x^2

a = 1/x^3 = x^(-3)

Therefore, n = 3

questions.text: Which of the following curves possibly represent one-dimensional motion of a particle?
questions.sol_text: For one-dimensional motion of a particle: (1) Phase vs time - Can be linear (valid). (2) Velocity vs displacement - Must form a closed loop or curve that doesn't repeat for same displacement (invalid - represents harmonic motion but velocity cannot have two values for same displacement in standard 1D motion plots). (3) Velocity vs time - Can form any curve including circular (valid). (4) Total distance vs time - Must be monotonically increasing (valid - distance never decreases). t(4t^2 - 3) = 0
